basis.governing_question: Should Quinta Azul enter the Spanish retail market and, if so, how?

sub_questions.question: How large and attractive is the Spanish retail market for Quinta Azul's olive oil?
Who competes for shelf space in Spanish retail, and what do buyers require from a supplier?
Does Quinta Azul have the assets and capabilities to win in Spanish retail?
Which entry option is best for Quinta Azul, and does its business case support a go?
What roadmap would take Quinta Azul into Spanish retail if the answer is go?

work.unit: Market assessed in full (demand, channels, competitors, regulation, buyer interviews)

phase_work.why: One market assessed in full, no screening step; capability and client interview work run alongside the market work.

work.unit: Entry option and business case for one market
Entry sequence and roadmap across markets

phase_work.why: Business case for the single market first, then the entry roadmap; with one market the roadmap sequences entry steps, not markets.

sizing.levers: A narrower scope, such as one retail channel, would shorten Research most; drafting the roadmap alongside the business case would shorten Design.

phases.name: Research
phases.objective_one_line: Establish how attractive the Spanish retail market is and whether Quinta Azul can win there.

gate.label: Go/no-go on design
gate.decision: Take Spain forward to entry design, or stop here?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define Quinta Azul's entry options for Spain, the case for the preferred one and the entry roadmap.

gate.label: Final decision
gate.decision: Approve the go or no-go on Spain and, if go, the entry plan?

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given; the 7 to 10 weeks are an estimate for one market, to be confirmed before quoting.
The estimate assumes capability work and CEO and Commercial Director interviews run alongside market work; in sequence, Research grows by 1 to 2 weeks.
